newsitem.title: GERMANY: Union Investment sees lower funds sales in 95/96.
newsitem.headline: Union Investment sees lower funds sales in 95/96.

text.p: Germany's fourth-largest fund management group, Union Investment GmbH, said late on Monday that it had seen lower fund sales in the year to the end of September, despite higher returns from funds under management.
The total amount managed by Union Investment in the year was 45.5 billion marks ($30.3 billion), up from 42.5 billion marks in the previous year, an increase of seven percent.

"From the company's point of view it has to be said that the seven percent increase in fund's assets was chiefly the result of the positive performance of the funds," said Manfred Mathes, managing director of Union Investments.
The company described the growth in its funds as "above-average, on a year-on-year basis".
Among individual equity-based funds, Union's EM Eastern Europe fund was the top performer among its funds with a return of 42 percent.
This was followed by its EuroAction fund, with returns of 29.5 percent since it was issued. The UniNorthAmerica fund was in third place with returns of 26.5 percent.
Union said its bond-based funds gained from increases on German and European debt markets.
Its internationally-invested UniRenta bond-based fund increased by 13.8 percent over the year, while its best-performing German bond-based fund was UniBond L, which saw returns of 11 percent.

"Net inflows, at 389 million marks, stayed modest. That the Union group is in fourth place among German fund management companies is poor consolation. However, this figure does mask the intensity of business during the year, and gross sales hit a record level of 17.9 billion marks," said Mathes.

Gerhard Langenbach, member of the management board, said that Union had received around 100 million marks worth of shares in Deutsche Telekom during its flotation on Monday, around a third of what it had sought to buy.
Langenbach said: "We won't be buying any more for the moment, but we will be having a look first to see how the share price does. There are other international telecoms shares which are cheaper."
Union Investment is owned by a consortium of private and cooperative banks. Its figures for 1995/96 put it into twelfth place among European fund management companies.
